# `Q-2-61` — Unquoted attribute value containing a comma

> Attribute values containing `,` must be quoted. Write `widths="1,3"`
> rather than `widths=1,3`.

## What this means

In an attribute block such as `{.class key=value}`, an unquoted value
may only contain characters that cannot be confused with the rest of
the attribute syntax. A comma is not one of them, so a value that
contains one has to be wrapped in quotes.

## Why this happens

Comma-separated settings copied from an extension's documentation, for
example a list table's column widths or alignments:

```markdown
::: {.list-table widths=1,3 aligns=l,c}
- - A
  - B
:::
```

The same applies to attribute blocks on spans, images, inline code and
headings.

Because the parser cannot tell where the attribute block ends, it
cannot reliably read the rest of the file either, so Quarto reports
only this error and none that come after it.

## How to fix

Quote the value:

```markdown
::: {.list-table widths="1,3" aligns="l,c"}
- - A
  - B
:::
```
